22.0.s.en: (1) Balaam's refusal to curse the people as Balak requested

22.0.0.en: The plains of Moab: the word "plain" (Arabah) means a waste or a place dominated by desert nature, and the word "plains" means an extended and desolate region, and it was applied to the whole region from the Gulf of Aqaba in the south to the Dead Sea in its middle and then the river Jordan to the north, and the expression "plains of Moab" means the region in which the tribes of the Moabites dwell (map 4). On this side Jordan by Jericho: the word "side" (ebar) means "the bank or shore of the river," and "on this side Jordan by Jericho" means the eastern bank of the Jordan opposite the city of Jericho.

22.0.1.en: After the victories of the children of Israel over the Amorites, they journeyed northward alongside the eastern bank, and when they were opposite Jericho, which lies on the western bank of the river Jordan, "Balak" king of Moab, whose lands extend alongside the Dead Sea to the south and the river Jordan to the north on the eastern side, saw them, and he was distressed and greatly terrified at the sight of the people and their great number on the one hand, and at what the people had done to "Sihon" and "Og" on the other.

22.1.0.en: Expressing his fear and dread, "Balak" gathered the chiefs of his people and his wise men of the Moabites and some elders of the Midianites who were pasturing their livestock in the lands of the Moabites, and said to them that this people is very numerous and that all the good things of our lands and our farms are not enough to feed them. The use of the expression "lick up" means that it will consume everything and there will be left for us no greenery or crops to eat after it, for it will leave the land bare.

22.2.0.en: Balaam the son of Beor: he is the same as Balaam the son of Bosor (2 Pet 2:15), and opinions differ about his person. Some regarded him as a diviner who followed Satan, because of the saying of Joshua the son of Nun, "Balaam also the son of Beor, the soothsayer" (Josh 13:22), but most commentators regarded him as a prophet of the Lord whom God used to deliver some messages to the peoples of the region, and this is confirmed by the following events in this chapter ... But although he was a prophet, the Holy Bible afterward describes him as betraying and allying with the enemies of the people for the sake of money, although he blessed the people with his mouth as God first commanded him (ch. 23). Pethor: the name of the village where Balaam lived, and it lies on the western bank of the river Euphrates. So Balaam was a prophet, but not of the children of Israel, but living among the Gentiles.

22.2.1.en: The land of the children of his people: that is, present-day Iraq.

22.2.2.en: A people come out from Egypt: that is, the people of Israel.

22.2.3.en: Balak sent messengers to Balaam at his place of residence, and they told him of his fears of the very numerous people of the children of Israel who had come out of Egypt and now stood in their full number before the borders of the Moabites.

22.3.0.en: The content of Balak's message was an invitation to Balaam to come and curse this numerous people, for Balak and the Amorites had no ability to fight it, but if Balaam cursed it, Balak would be able to defeat the children of Israel and drive them out of the whole region. And Balak adds in his message, as a kind of praise for Balaam, that it is known of him that whoever he blesses is blessed, and whoever he curses is cursed by God.

22.4.0.en: The rewards of divination: that is, a gift and reward in return for his divination or his cursing of the people, and its colloquial meaning, which some people still use, is "the sweets" given in return for good news. As for the word divination, its meaning by itself is knowledge of the unseen.

22.4.1.en: The delegates and messengers of Balak, from the elders of the Moabites and the Midianites, came with a valuable gift to Balaam and told him all that Balak had said before ... As for Balaam's reply to them, it was not hasty, but he asked them to lodge overnight so that he might pray to God and learn His opinion ... From this it appears that Balaam was wavering between obedience to God and love of money, which will appear afterward.

22.4.2.en: Would that you not hurry or give an answer about an opinion or counsel before you lift your heart to God in a quick prayer.

22.5.0.en: And God came unto Balaam: it may have been in a vision, or God sent him an angel.

22.5.1.en: Although God knew all the events, in His message to Balaam He asks him like one inquiring about something, "What men are these with thee?", in order to alert Balaam so that he would be on guard against the events to come.

22.6.0.en: Balaam's answer came as a faithful summary of what had come before in verses (5-7).

22.7.0.en: As for God's reply to Balaam's words, it was decisive and clear, for He told him plainly not to go with them and not to curse the people, and God made clear to him that it is a blessed people and that God Himself is the cause and secret of its blessing.

22.8.0.en: Balaam's answer to the messengers of Balak came exactly as the Lord had commanded him, for he refused to go to their lands, making clear that God had forbidden him, so the chiefs returned to Balak without Balaam and told him of his refusal to come with them.

22.8.1.en: It is to be noted that Balaam told the messengers of Balak all of God's words, which is His saying that the people of Israel is blessed by God, and perhaps he had become attached to Balak's gifts and wished that he would send to him again with new gifts.

22.9.s.en: (2) The second delegation from Balak to Balaam

22.9.0.en: Balak did not despair at Balaam's first refusal, so he returned and sent him a delegation more numerous and of higher rank and standing, and the message of this delegation to Balaam was that he should come down with them to meet Balak and curse the people of the children of Israel. The delegation enticed him by saying that Balak would honor him very greatly, meaning of course gifts and monetary offerings, and that he would also carry out for him any wish or request.

22.10.0.en: Balaam's answer was unexpected by the delegation sent to him, for he appeared decisive and clear and refused the offer and enticement, whatever was offered to him of money, gold or silver, and he declared his unwillingness to go against God's word to satisfy Balak's wish. This shows the good side in him, that is, his holding to obedience to God, if only outwardly, although he would afterward devise a way to disobey it.

22.11.0.en: Despite Balaam's sound position in the preceding verse, it carried more pretense than sincerity, and here his heart began to expose him, for he knew already that it was God who had prevented him from cursing the people and from going with them. But this last offer from Balak swayed his heart, and therefore he proposed to the messengers that they stay with him overnight, perhaps that God would bring him something new other than what He had said to him before, that is, he was not decisive in refusing their new invitation and their gifts.

22.11.1.en: Very often this happens to us ... when God's will is perfectly clear in some matter, but because of our own wicked or self-serving will we argue with ourselves, hoping that God has another opinion, and perhaps we ask many people in roundabout ways until we get an answer that agrees with what we want and not what God wants... Reject enticement and weakness and listen to the voice of God within you.

22.12.0.en: God spoke with Balaam by night and permitted him to go with the men, but He set him a condition that he speak only what God commanded him.

22.12.2.en: Perhaps we ask why God permitted Balaam to go after he had refused at first?!!

22.12.3.en: First: because God knew well that what Balaam had uttered was not what was within him, for the lust for money had stirred in him.

22.12.4.en: Second: God had a plan through which He wanted to teach him a lesson, and we shall see that in the coming verses. Third: God's plan also included that Balaam bless the people instead of cursing them before Balak, so that Balak would be certain that this people is the people of God, who enjoys His protection.

22.13.0.en: Balaam rose in the morning and saddled his donkey and set out with the messengers to meet Balak.

22.14.s.en: (3) Balaam and his meeting with the angel of the Lord on the way

22.14.0.en: His two servants: two of his slaves.

22.14.1.en: Balaam took two of his slaves with him on the way to meet Balak, and while he was riding on his she ass, the angel of the Lord stood in his way and stopped before him, and the inspired Word indicates that God was angry at Balaam's conduct because his heart was attached to the love of money, and God had agreed to his going in order to test his heart. So the appearance of the angel and his rebuke of him was an opportunity for his repentance, as we explained before, and the time of the lesson had come here, and God's showing His displeasure.

22.15.0.en: The angel appeared in a fearful sight, for he carried a drawn sword in his hand, and the remarkable thing is that the one who saw him was the donkey and not Balaam the prophet. Of course this was by divine arrangement, that the angel should appear to the donkey without Balaam seeing him, in order that God might show us the blindness of the man whose eyes money and gold have shut, so that he does not see God nor hear His voice. And the she ass was disturbed by the fearful sight and left the road and turned aside into the field, and Balaam struck her to bring her back to the road.

22.16.0.en: A path of the vineyards: a narrow road or passage between two walls, roofed by a grape trellis.

22.16.1.en: During the journey the she ass passed through a narrow passage, and when she saw the angel and his sword again she was terrified and leaned toward one of the two walls, and as she leaned she pressed against the leg and foot of Balaam, who of course was angered at the conduct of the she ass and struck her a second time.

22.17.1.en: She fell down: she lay down.

22.17.2.en: In another place on the road, which was still narrower, the angel stood again before the she ass, in a place where she could not turn to the right or to the left, so she stopped walking altogether, and therefore Balaam was very angry and struck her a third time, and more violently.

22.18.1.en: We now stand before a great divine miracle, for God by His power made the animal speak with Balaam, and the speech came in the form of a reproach, as the animal asked the man why he had struck her three times. We do not know Balaam's reaction when he heard the animal speak, but we believe it was a mixture of astonishment and fear, yet this did not prevent Balaam from speaking with the she ass and answering her that he struck her because she had disobeyed him three times in walking, and he added that he was very angry with her and that she deserved to be killed and not merely struck.

22.19.0.en: Continuing the dialogue, the she ass replies to Balaam again, trying to draw his attention to her constant obedience to him since he had owned her before this day, and she asked him whether she had ever rebelled against him before, and he answered no.

22.19.1.en: The message is clear to all of us through these events, by which God wants to rebuke Balaam, as if He were telling him that the dumb animal obeyed My will, but you, O man, since evil filled your heart, did not understand and did not see what the animal saw!!!!!!

22.19.2.en: May we, when we are exposed to afflictions, examine ourselves so as to repent of our sins and learn from the events of life and even from animals as well.

22.20.0.en: God opened Balaam's eyes, and he saw the angel and his drawn sword, and then he was so afraid that he got down from his donkey and bowed before the angel.

22.21.0.en: Thy way is perverse before me: the way is thorny and leads to destruction.

22.21.1.en: To withstand: to prevent, hinder and warn.

22.21.2.en: The angel spoke to Balaam, making clear to him that his appearing to him was to prevent him from going and cursing the people, and he makes clear that the hidden things of his heart, that is, his love of money, are exposed before God. He also rebukes him for striking his she ass three times without cause, and that the she ass was better than he spiritually, since she saw the angel whom he did not see because of his evil. And the angel adds, in his defense of the struck she ass, that if she had not done so, the angel of the Lord would have killed him and spared the she ass.

22.22.0.en: Balaam offered an immediate apology to the angel of the Lord, making clear to him that he had not seen him, otherwise he would not have struck the she ass three times, and, completing his apology, he declared his immediate readiness not to complete his journey to Balak and to return to his house; but the angel commanded him to complete his journey, though he must not say anything of his own but speak what the Spirit of God would tell him by means of the angel, and therefore Balaam completed his journey with the messengers of Balak.

22.22.1.en: Balaam carried many contradictions in his character, yet it must not escape us here to highlight his quick response of repentance and apology. For the word "I have sinned" that he said was the cause of his deliverance from punishment, while Adam did not utter it when he fell!!! May we all learn to apologize quickly for error and not justify ourselves, for the word "I have sinned" calms the anger of the one we have wronged and makes God have pity on our weakness.

22.23.0.en: One of Balak's messengers went ahead of the procession and told him of Balaam's coming this time, and in his great joy at this news Balak went out quickly to receive Balaam at the farthest border of his country, as is done in receiving great men. He did not wait for him to enter the land of the Moabites but went out himself to the border, and at the first city of the Moabites, called "a city of Moab," which lies on the border at the small river Arnon, he received Balaam.

22.24.0.en: Balak was first to greet Balaam and speak, and in a gentle reproach he asked him, did I not send for you before? Why then did you not come? And now that you have come, shall I not honor you and give you abundant reward?

22.25.0.en: Balaam answered that he was here now and this was what mattered, and under the effect of his fear from the sight of the angel whom he had seen a little while before, he added to Balak that he would not be able to speak anything but what God says to him.

22.26.0.en: Balaam went with Balak to a village named "Kirjath-huzoth," one of the cities of Moab and the first city fit to receive and honor Balaam and those with him, and it lies north of the river Arnon, and Balak was very generous, for he slaughtered for the feast in honor of Balaam many oxen and sheep, although the number of men was small, but he wanted to show Balaam the extent of his generosity as an indication of what Balaam would get of gifts and gold if he cursed the people, and it also shows the warmth of the reception of this great guest.

22.27.0.en: The high places of Baal: the name of a high and elevated place, like a plateau, which was called "Baal."

22.27.1.en: Because they used to sacrifice to Baal on it, that is, they offered worship to Baal as one of the pagan worships (map 6). The chain of mountains of Abarim, Shittim. Map (6). After spending a night of honor and rest, Balak took Balaam in the early morning to a high place, the "high places of Baal," and showed him the people from there, and because the place was high Balaam was able to see all the people to the farthest point of their encampment.

22.27.2.en: The enticements of the world are many to distract you from God's commandments, but on the other hand God warns you so that you do not perish with this wicked world, as the angel warned Balaam, so hold fast to God's commandments, and do not run after the dazzling allurements of the world, for all of them are passing away, and if you have become preoccupied with them, hasten to return to God and set limits to your attachment to the world.

22.27.3.en: The discourses (parables) of Balaam, an introduction:

22.27.4.en: In this chapter and the one after it (ch. 24) we find four discourses that Balaam uttered about the people of Israel and then a prophecy about other peoples. This chapter includes the first and second of them, while the coming chapter includes the third and fourth.
